title.zh: 卷424 列傳二百十一 吴振棫 张亮基 毛鸿宾 张凯嵩
title.en: Volume 424 Biographies 211: Wu Zhenyu, Zhang Liangji, Mao Hongbin, Zhang Kaisong
title.raw: 卷424 列傳二百十一 吴振棫 张亮基 毛鸿宾 张凯嵩

sentences.zh: =吳振棫=吳振棫，字仲雲，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: =Wu Zhenyu= Wu Zhenyu, courtesy name Zhongyun, a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: =Wu Zhenyu= Wu Zhenyu, courtesy name Zhongyun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the nineteenth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，出為雲南大理知府，歷山東登州、沂州、濟南，安徽鳳陽知府；

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was sent out as prefect of Dali in Yunnan, and successively served as prefect of Dengzhou, Yizhou, and Jinan in Shandong, and of Fengyang in Anhui;
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was posted as prefect of Dali in Yunnan, and later served successively as prefect of Dengzhou, Yizhou, and Jinan in Shandong and of Fengyang in Anhui;

sentences.zh: 山東登萊青道；

translations.literal: intendant of the Deng-Lai-Qing Circuit in Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: as intendant of the Deng-Lai-Qing Circuit in Shandong;

sentences.zh: 貴州糧儲道；

translations.literal: grain intendant of Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: as grain intendant of Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 貴州按察使；

translations.literal: judicial commissioner of Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: as judicial commissioner of Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 山西、四川布政使。

translations.literal: and provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: and finally as provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was promoted to governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was promoted to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 尋甸、東川回匪蠢動，粵匪由廣西闌入開化、廣南境，偕總督吳文鎔先後遣將擊平之。

translations.literal: Hui rebels stirred in Xundian and Dongchuan, and Guangdong bandits from Guangxi broke into the districts of Kaihua and Guangnan; together with Governor-General Wu Wenrong he successively dispatched generals to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui rebels rose in Xundian and Dongchuan and Guangdong bandits from Guangxi invaded Kaihua and Guangnan, he and Governor-General Wu Wenrong sent troops in succession until both disturbances were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 四年，調陝西巡撫，未行，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to be governor of Shaanxi; before he departed he served as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he was transferred to Shaanxi as governor, but before he could take up the post he acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貴州興義、普安匪起，檄安義鎮總兵金剛保等剿之。

translations.literal: Rebels rose in Xingyi and Pu'an in Guizhou; he issued orders to Regional Commander Jin Gangbao of the Anyi garrison and others to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke out in Xingyi and Pu'an in Guizhou, he ordered Regional Commander Jin Gangbao of the Anyi garrison and others to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 遵義亦被匪圍，合滇、黔兵力，迭戰獲勝，擒匪首楊鳳先於石阡葛莊司。

translations.literal: Zunyi was also besieged by rebels; combining the forces of Yunnan and Guizhou, he won repeated victories in battle and captured the rebel leader Yang Fengxian at Gezhuang Subprefecture in Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyi too came under rebel siege; he combined Yunnan and Guizhou troops, won a series of victories, and captured the rebel leader Yang Fengxian at Gezhuang in Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，始抵陝西任。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year he finally arrived to take up his post in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the autumn of 1855 did he finally reach Shaanxi to assume office.

sentences.zh: 匪首陳通明受粵匪指揮，於潼關糾眾謀響應，以計擒之，並獲其黨張順、羅吉祥等置諸法，被詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Chen Tongming, acting under Guangdong bandit orders, gathered a crowd at Tong Pass to plot a coordinated rising; by stratagem he was captured, and his followers Zhang Shun, Luo Jixiang, and others were seized and punished by law; an imperial edict commended the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Chen Tongming, directed by Guangdong bandits, mustered men at Tong Pass to join the uprising; Zhenyu captured him by stratagem, seized his associates Zhang Shun and Luo Jixiang, and had them executed, for which he received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 鹽課攤歸地丁，數倍於昔，奏請改行招販，先課后鹽，民便之。

translations.literal: The salt levy had been folded into the land-and-poll tax and was several times what it had been; he memorialized to change to licensed private sale, collecting the tax before the salt, which the people found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Because the salt tax folded into the land-and-poll assessment had risen several fold, he memorialized for licensed private salt sales with tax collected before delivery, a reform the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢四川總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 七年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南漢、回積仇，自中原兵事亟，協餉不至，回亂愈恣。

translations.literal: In Yunnan Han and Hui bore long-standing enmity; since warfare in the central provinces was urgent, coordinated funds did not arrive, and the Hui rebellion grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was torn by long-standing Han-Hui hatred; with the empire consumed by war in the central provinces, relief funds never arrived, and the Hui rebellion grew worse.

sentences.zh: 團練跋扈，動相殺掠，省城戒嚴。

translations.literal: The local militia were overbearing and constantly killed and plundered one another; the provincial capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia ran rampant, killing and looting at will, and the provincial capital was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 前任總督恆春不能制，夫婦同縊，巡撫舒興阿亦以病求去，惟布政使桑春榮困守危城。

translations.literal: The former governor-general Hengchun could not control them and he and his wife hanged themselves together; Governor Shu Xing'a also asked to leave on grounds of illness; only Provincial Administration Commissioner Sang Chunrong remained trapped defending the endangered city.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor-General Hengchun proved unable to restore order and hanged himself with his wife; Governor Shu Xing'a resigned on grounds of illness; only Provincial Administration Commissioner Sang Chunrong remained, holding the besieged capital.

sentences.zh: 文宗知振棫熟悉滇省情形，故以代之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong knew that Zhenyu was familiar with conditions in Yunnan, and therefore replaced him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Zhenyu's familiarity with Yunnan, Emperor Wenzong appointed him to replace Hengchun.

sentences.zh: 命選川兵三千，攜餉五萬馳往，調前山東巡撫張亮基幫辦軍務以副之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to select three thousand Sichuan troops and hurry there with fifty thousand taels of funds, and the former governor of Shandong Zhang Liangji was transferred to assist in military affairs as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take three thousand Sichuan troops and fifty thousand taels of silver to Yunnan, with former Shandong Governor Zhang Liangji assigned to assist him in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 振或至，先駐宣威，進次​​曲靖。

translations.literal: When Zhenyu arrived he first encamped at Xuanwei and then advanced to Qujing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyu arrived he first halted at Xuanwei and then advanced to Qujing.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「先剿後撫，勢順而易，不待智者而知。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "To suppress first and pacify afterward follows the easier course of events, as anyone of sense knows.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Suppress first and pacify afterward—that is the easier course, and needs no sage to see it.

sentences.zh: 兵盛餉足，必應如是。

translations.literal: With abundant troops and ample funds, one must act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: With ample troops and funds, that is surely the right course.

sentences.zh: 前督臣林則徐剿永昌回匪，兵、練萬餘，本省有餉可籌；

translations.literal: Former Governor Lin Zexu suppressed the Hui rebels of Yongchang with more than ten thousand regulars and militia, and funds could be raised within the province;
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Lin Zexu suppressed the Hui rebels of Yongchang, he had more than ten thousand regulars and militia and could raise supplies within the province;

sentences.zh: 彌渡獲勝，匪旋受撫，其地祗迤西一隅中之一隅。

translations.literal: victory at Midu was won and the rebels soon submitted to pacification; that region was only one corner within one corner of western Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: after victory at Midu the rebels soon submitted; that trouble was confined to a single corner of western Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 此次匪遍三迤，情形迥不相同，非數千之兵、十數万之餉所能蕆事。

translations.literal: This time rebels spread throughout the three circuits of western Yunnan; the situation is utterly different and cannot be brought to completion with only a few thousand troops and one or two hundred thousand taels of funds.
translations.idiomatic: Now rebels roam all three western circuits of Yunnan—a wholly different situation that cannot be settled with a few thousand men and a hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 如率意迳行，徒損國威，於事無補。

translations.literal: If one proceeds rashly and directly, one will only harm national prestige without helping the matter.
translations.idiomatic: To rush ahead regardless would only damage imperial prestige without advancing the cause.

sentences.zh: 臣初到滇，於漢、回兩無嫌怨，惟憑藉兵威，結以恩信，有所申訴，處以公平。

translations.literal: When your servant first reached Yunnan he bore no grudge against either Han or Hui; he relied on military prestige and bound them with kindness and trust; when there were petitions he dealt with them fairly.
translations.idiomatic: When I first reached Yunnan I bore no grudge against either Han or Hui; I would rely on military strength, win them with kindness and trust, and judge every petition fairly.

sentences.zh: 省城為根本重地，省回解散，此外漸次籌辦，其負嵎抗拒者，仍當力剿。

translations.literal: The provincial capital is the fundamental stronghold; the Hui within the province should be disbanded, and beyond that matters should be handled step by step; those who cling to resistance must still be vigorously suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the root of the province: disband the Hui there first, then handle the rest step by step, while still crushing those who stubbornly resist.

sentences.zh: 匪勢漸孤，較易得手。

translations.literal: The rebel power would gradually be isolated and would be easier to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels would grow isolated and be easier to defeat.

sentences.zh: 否則不自量度而急乘之，更無轉圜地步，禍更烈矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, without measuring one's strength and pressing the attack in haste, there would be no room to turn back, and the calamity would grow fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, if we overreach and press the attack, there will be no room to retreat and the disaster will only worsen.

sentences.zh: 現在兵無可調，餉無可籌，宵旰焦勞，事非一省。

translations.literal: At present no troops can be mobilized and no funds raised; the emperor toils early and late in anxiety, and the matter is not that of a single province alone.
translations.idiomatic: At present there are no troops to mobilize and no funds to raise; the emperor labors in ceaseless anxiety, and this is not a crisis for Yunnan alone.

sentences.zh: 臣為雲南一省計，並當為天下全局計，豈容再有貽誤，致令徵調無休？

translations.literal: Your servant plans for Yunnan as one province and must also plan for the empire as a whole; how can there be further delay causing endless levies of troops?
translations.idiomatic: I must plan for Yunnan and for the empire as a whole; how can we risk another mistake that would bring endless troop levies?

sentences.zh: 故未言剿先言撫，有萬不得已之苦衷，雖成敗利鈍難以逆料，捨此亦別無良策也。」

translations.literal: Therefore before speaking of suppression he spoke of pacification, with an anguish of utter necessity; though success or failure and gain or loss cannot be foretold, apart from this there is no other good plan."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I speak of pacification before suppression—not from choice but from necessity; though the outcome cannot be foreseen, I see no better course."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「在籍侍郎黃琮、御史竇墉、總兵周鳳岐奉命團練，設總局於省城。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Retired Vice President Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were ordered to organize local militia and established a general bureau in the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported: "Retired Vice President Huang Cong, Censor Dou Yong, and Regional Commander Zhou Fengqi were ordered to organize militia and set up a general bureau in the capital.

sentences.zh: 周鳳岐意見不合，引嫌不肯與聞。

translations.literal: Zhou Fengqi disagreed in opinion and, citing scruple, refused to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fengqi disagreed with their views and, pleading conflict of interest, refused to participate.

sentences.zh: 黃琮、竇墉聯銜出示，專主痛剿，民間紛紛集練，回眾疑忌日深。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and Dou Yong jointly issued proclamations, insisting solely on fierce suppression; the populace rushed to form militia companies, and suspicion among the Hui grew deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong and Dou Yong issued joint proclamations calling for ruthless suppression; civilians rushed to form militia bands, and Hui suspicion deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 地方官苦心解散，漢民往往閧堂塞署，逼官殺回。

translations.literal: Local officials labored to disband them, yet Han civilians often stormed the yamen and blocked the offices, forcing officials to kill Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials struggled to disband the militia, but Han mobs often stormed government offices and forced officials to kill Hui.

sentences.zh: 故團練在他省為要務，在滇省竟為大患。

translations.literal: Thus whereas local militia were an essential measure in other provinces, in Yunnan they became a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: What was an essential tool in other provinces became a grave disaster in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 黃琮等每言省團可得六十萬人，無虞寇警。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and others constantly said the provincial militia could muster six hundred thousand men and that there was no need to fear bandit alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong and his allies claimed the provincial militia could field six hundred thousand men and that bandits need not be feared.

sentences.zh: 回匪初至城外，不及千人，團丁招之不來，來即奔潰。

translations.literal: When the Hui rebels first reached outside the city walls there were fewer than a thousand; militiamen could not be summoned to come, and when they did come they fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hui rebels first appeared outside the walls there were fewer than a thousand; militiamen would not answer the call, and those who did fled at once.

sentences.zh: 近日省練一萬餘人，月需餉數万，經費不敷。

translations.literal: Recently the provincial militia numbered more than ten thousand; each month they required tens of thousands in pay, and funds were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The capital militia now exceed ten thousand men and cost tens of thousands of taels a month—far beyond available funds.

sentences.zh: 練頭自行管帶，不盡官派。

translations.literal: Militia leaders commanded their own men and were not wholly appointed by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Militia leaders commanded their own followers rather than answering fully to official appointment.

sentences.zh: 回眾有求撫之意，梗議者忽用練往剿，妄殺邀功，致可撫者終不能撫。

translations.literal: The Hui had a mind to seek pacification, but obstructionists suddenly sent militia to suppress them, killing recklessly to claim merit, so that those who could have been pacified could never in the end be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Many Hui were ready to submit, but hard-liners sent militia against them, killing indiscriminately for credit, so that those who might have been pacified never could be.

sentences.zh: 黃琮、竇墉系特派人員，非臣力所能製，請旨定奪。

translations.literal: Huang Cong and Dou Yong were specially dispatched personnel, beyond what your servant's strength could control; he begged an imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Cong and Dou Yong were imperial appointees beyond my authority to restrain; I beg Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 臣已諮桑春榮嚴覈守城之練，裁汰冗濫，以節糜費。

translations.literal: Your servant had already instructed Sang Chunrong strictly to examine the militia defending the city, cut redundant and excessive numbers, and economize wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: I have already instructed Sang Chunrong to audit the capital garrison militia strictly, cut redundant numbers, and curb waste.

sentences.zh: 練歸官統，如不奉調派，自行出隊，即按軍法從事，庶一事權而免掣肘。」

translations.literal: The militia should return to official command; if they did not obey orders for deployment and went out on their own, they would be dealt with by military law, so that authority might be unified and hindrance avoided."
translations.idiomatic: Militia must return to official command; any who march out without orders should face military law, so that authority is unified and interference ended."

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔褫黃琮、竇墉職，許回民悔悟自新，其負固不服者，痛加剿辦。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, an edict stripped Huang Cong and Dou Yong of their posts, permitted Hui people who repented and renewed themselves, and ordered fierce suppression of those who stubbornly refused submission.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court stripped Huang Cong and Dou Yong of office, allowed repentant Hui to reform, and ordered ruthless suppression of those who still resisted.

sentences.zh: 漢民借團練為名肆行殺掠者，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Han civilians who under the name of local militia carried out killing and plunder were to be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Han who used the militia as a cover for killing and looting were to face military justice.

sentences.zh: 於是振棫遣漢、回委員赴省城曉諭漢、回，解釋猜嫌，分畫所居街道，撥抵難民遺產，議定章程，遣散歸業。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhenyu sent Han and Hui commissioners to the provincial capital to instruct Han and Hui, explain away mutual suspicion, demarcate the streets where each lived, allocate refugee property in settlement, agree on regulations, and disperse them to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyu then sent Han and Hui commissioners to the capital to explain the settlement, assign residential streets, allocate abandoned property to refugees, set regulations, and send people home to their trades.

sentences.zh: 先後剿平霑益回匪，殲咸寧土匪李廣沅。

translations.literal: In succession he suppressed the Hui rebels of Zhanyi and destroyed the bandit of Xianning Li Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He successively suppressed the Hui rebels of Zhanyi and destroyed the Xianning bandit Li Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，撫局粗定，入駐省城，偕張亮基籌辦迤西剿撫事宜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year the pacification arrangements were roughly settled; he entered and garrisoned the provincial capital and, together with Zhang Liangji, planned the suppression and pacification affairs of western Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1858 the pacification was roughly in place; he moved into the capital and, with Zhang Liangji, organized suppression and pacification in western Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 臨安回匪攻府城，遣兵擊走之，又敗之於阿迷州，解河西縣之圍。

translations.literal: Hui rebels of Lin'an attacked the prefectural city; he sent troops to drive them off, defeated them again at Ami Prefecture, and relieved the siege of Hexi County.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin'an Hui rebels attacked the prefectural seat, he drove them off, defeated them at Ami, and lifted the siege of Hexi County.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以病乞罷，因子春傑官雁平道，就養山西。

translations.literal: That winter, on grounds of illness he asked to retire; because his son Chunjie held the post of Yanping Circuit intendant, he went to Shanxi to be supported in his old age.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he resigned on grounds of illness and went to Shanxi to live with his son Chunjie, who held the Yanping intendant post.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，命會同巡撫英桂防河，尋命赴陝西會辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was ordered to join Governor Yinggui in defending the Yellow River, and soon afterward was ordered to go to Shaanxi to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was ordered to join Governor Yinggui in river defense, and soon after was sent to Shaanxi to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，詔依例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict granted posthumous favors according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1871, and the court granted the usual posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: =張亮基=張亮基，字石卿，江蘇銅山人。

translations.literal: =Zhang Liangji= Zhang Liangji, courtesy name Shiqing, a native of Tongshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: =Zhang Liangji= Zhang Liangji, courtesy name Shiqing, was a native of Tongshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年舉人，入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination; by purchase of office he became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in 1834 and purchased appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從大學士王鼎赴河南治河，督築西壩。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Secretary Wang Ding to Henan to control the Yellow River and supervised construction of the western embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Grand Secretary Wang Ding to Henan for river control and supervised construction of the western embankment.

sentences.zh: 工竣，賜花翎，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: When the work was completed he was granted the peacock feather and promoted to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was finished he received the peacock feather and was promoted to Reader.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，出為雲南臨安知府，總督林則徐曾與共事河工，知其才，密薦可大用，調署永昌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was sent out as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; Governor-General Lin Zexu, who had worked with him on river projects, knew his talent and secretly recommended him for great employment; he was transferred to act as prefect of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he was posted as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; Governor-General Lin Zexu, who had worked with him on river projects, recognized his ability and secretly recommended him for higher office; he was transferred to act as prefect of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 邊夷滋擾，亮基用土弁左大雄擒匪首，事乃定。

translations.literal: Border tribes grew troublesome; Liangji used the native officer Zuo Daxiong to capture the rebel leader, and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When border tribes grew restless, Liangji used the native officer Zuo Daxiong to capture the rebel chief and restore order.

sentences.zh: 超擢雲南按察使，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted out of turn to judicial commissioner of Yunnan and then moved directly to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted out of turn to judicial commissioner of Yunnan and soon after to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢雲南巡撫，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan and also acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he became governor of Yunnan and also acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 粵匪漸熾，嘗密疏論軍事，文宗韙之。

translations.literal: Guangdong bandits grew ever stronger; he once submitted a secret memorial on military affairs, and Emperor Wenzong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: As Guangdong rebels grew stronger, he submitted a secret memorial on military affairs that Emperor Wenzong endorsed.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調湖南巡撫，在途聞賊圍長沙，疏請駐守常德。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to be governor of Hunan; on the road he heard that bandits were besieging Changsha and memorialized to garrison Changde.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was transferred to Hunan; en route he learned that rebels were besieging Changsha and memorialized to halt at Changde.

sentences.zh: 詔趣進解省城之圍，至則梯城而入，屢出隊與城外援軍夾擊，賊解圍去。

translations.literal: An edict urged him to advance and relieve the siege of the provincial capital; when he arrived he entered the city by scaling ladders, repeatedly led sorties to strike the bandits in concert with relief forces outside the walls, and the rebels lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to relieve Changsha, he entered the city by scaling ladders, led repeated sorties with outside relief forces, and drove the rebels away.

sentences.zh: 破岳州，入湖北，漢陽、武昌相繼陷，湖廣總督徐廣縉以罪罷，命亮基代之，規進剿。

translations.literal: They captured Yuezhou and entered Hubei; Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession; Governor-General of Huguang Xu Guangjin was dismissed for fault, and Liangji was ordered to replace him and plan an advance to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Yuezhou and swept into Hubei; Hanyang and Wuchang fell in turn; Governor-General Xu Guangjin was dismissed, and Liangji was appointed in his place to organize a counteroffensive.

sentences.zh: 亮基疏言宜防賊回竄，意在專顧湖南，詔趣速進。

translations.literal: Liangji memorialized that one should guard against the bandits doubling back, his intent being to concentrate on Hunan; an edict urged him to advance quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji argued for guarding against a rebel return into Hunan—a move seen as self-serving—and the court ordered him to advance at once.

sentences.zh: 三年春，賊棄武漢東下，亮基抵湖北籌辦收復撫卹事宜。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the bandits abandoned Wuhan and marched east; Liangji reached Hubei to arrange matters of recovery and relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1853 the rebels abandoned Wuhan and marched east; Liangji reached Hubei to organize recovery and relief.

sentences.zh: 通城、崇陽、嘉魚、廣濟土匪起，平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, and Guangji; he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed bandit outbreaks in Tongcheng, Chongyang, Jiayu, and Guangji.

sentences.zh: 賊自下游分竄江西，亮基督師扼道士洑、黃石港，分兵赴援。

translations.literal: Bandits from downstream split off and raided Jiangxi; Liangji personally led troops to hold Daoshifu and Huangshigang and sent detachments to aid.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel detachments from downstream raided Jiangxi, Liangji personally held Daoshifu and Huangshigang and sent troops to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 秋，賊之分竄河南者，由羅山入湖北黃安、麻城境，水陸夾擊，殲之。

translations.literal: In autumn the bandit detachment that had split into Henan entered the territory of Huang'an and Macheng in Hubei by way of Luoshan; he attacked them by land and water and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a rebel column from Henan entered Huang'an and Macheng in Hubei via Luoshan; he destroyed them in a combined land-and-water attack.

sentences.zh: 調山東巡撫，未行，江西賊由九江來犯，令道員徐豐玉御之於田家鎮，戰失利，豐玉陣亡，亮基坐降四級留任。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Shandong; before he departed, Jiangxi bandits came from Jiujiang to attack; he ordered Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu to resist them at Tianjiazhen; the battle was lost and Fengyu died in action; Liangji was demoted four ranks but retained his post.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shandong before he could leave, he sent Circuit Intendant Xu Fengyu to meet Jiangxi rebels from Jiujiang at Tianjiazhen; the battle was lost and Fengyu was killed; Liangji was demoted four ranks but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪李開芳等犯畿輔，踞靜海。

translations.literal: At that time Guangdong bandits Li Kaifang and others invaded the metropolitan region and occupied Jinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Kaifang and other Guangdong rebels invaded the capital region and occupied Jinghai.

sentences.zh: 亮基至山東，奉命扼德州，防其南逸。

translations.literal: When Liangji reached Shandong he was ordered to hold Dezhou and prevent the rebels from escaping south.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Shandong, Liangji was ordered to hold Dezhou and block a southern escape.

sentences.zh: 南路賊欲由淮、徐窺伺北犯為應援，令按察使厲恩官率兵駐宿遷之北以防之。

translations.literal: Southern-route bandits wished to watch for an opportunity through Huai and Xu to raid north in support; he ordered Judicial Commissioner Li En'guan to lead troops to encamp north of Suqian to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Southern rebels sought to move north through Huai and Xu in support; he stationed Judicial Commissioner Li En'guan north of Suqian to block them.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊入山東境，亮基馳扼濟寧，杜其北竄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year bandits entered Shandong territory; Liangji hurried to hold Jining and block their flight north.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 rebels entered Shandong; Liangji rushed to Jining to block their northward flight.

sentences.zh: 尋陷鄆城，擾範縣、壽張、東平，繞出賊前截擊，敗之於臨清黑家莊。

translations.literal: Soon they captured Yancheng and harassed Fan County, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he circled ahead of the bandits to intercept and defeated them at Heijiazhuang in Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: They soon took Yancheng and raided Fan, Shouzhang, and Dongping; he cut ahead of them and defeated them at Heijiazhuang near Linqing.

sentences.zh: 既奏捷，幫辦軍務大臣勝保劾其取巧冒功，詔斥亮基欺罔，並追論初赴湖南不急趨長沙，及去湖北時但求自全，居心狡詐，職，遣戍軍台。

translations.literal: After he reported victory, Grand Minister for Assisting in Military Affairs Sheng Bao impeached him for seizing credit by trickery; an edict rebuked Liangji for deception, and also reviewed how when he first went to Hunan he did not hurry to Changsha, and when he left Hubei he sought only to save himself, his heart being crafty; he was dismissed from office and sent in exile to the military garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After he reported victory, Sheng Bao accused him of claiming false credit; the court denounced Liangji as deceitful, cited his delay in relieving Changsha and his self-preservation in Hubei, dismissed him, and sent him to exile at the military garrison.

sentences.zh: 逾年，給事中毛鴻賓言臨清之役，勝保妄劾，御史宗稷辰亦言亮基能任事，未盡其用，乃釋回，發東河差遣，尋命往安徽隨辦軍務。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Supervising Secretary Mao Hongbin stated that in the battle of Linqing Sheng Bao had impeached falsely; Censor Zong Jichen also said Liangji was capable of bearing responsibility and had not been fully used; he was then released and returned, assigned to the Eastern River service, and soon ordered to Anhui to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Mao Hongbin argued that Sheng Bao's impeachment over Linqing was false, and Zong Jichen said Liangji was capable and underused; he was released, assigned to the Eastern River service, and soon sent to assist military affairs in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 七年，予五品頂戴，命赴雲南幫辦剿匪事宜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was granted the fifth-rank official cap button and ordered to go to Yunnan to assist in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he received the fifth-rank cap button and was ordered to Yunnan to assist in suppressing rebels.

sentences.zh: 雲南迴匪方熾，團練橫行省會，總督吳振棫初至，駐曲靖，裁抑練勇，招撫回眾。

translations.literal: Hui rebels in Yunnan were then raging; local militia ran rampant in the provincial capital; Governor-General Wu Zhenyu had just arrived, encamped at Qujing, curtailed militia forces, and summoned the Hui to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebels were raging in Yunnan and militia terrorized the capital; Governor-General Wu Zhenyu had just arrived at Qujing, where he curbed the militia and sought to pacify the Hui.

sentences.zh: 霑益回最悍，集眾犯宣威，亮基督按察使徐之銘等率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The Hui of Zhanyi were the fiercest; they gathered a host and attacked Xuanwei; Liangji personally led Judicial Commissioner Xu Zhiming and others to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhanyi Hui were the fiercest; when they attacked Xuanwei, Liangji led Judicial Commissioner Xu Zhiming and others to repulse them.

sentences.zh: 八年春，又敗之於袁家屯，殲賊甚眾，餘黨就撫，詔嘉之，授雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he defeated them again at Yuanjiatun, destroyed a great number of bandits, and the remnant submitted to pacification; an edict commended him and appointed him governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1858 he defeated them again at Yuanjiatun, killed many rebels, and received the surrender of the rest; the court commended him and appointed him governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 既而振棫乞罷，擢雲貴總督，亮基薦徐之銘代為巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhenyu asked to retire; Liangji was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, and Liangji recommended Xu Zhiming to replace him as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyu resigned, Liangji was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou and recommended Xu Zhiming as governor.

sentences.zh: 臨安回匪攻城，擾及阿迷，剿平之。

translations.literal: Lin'an Hui rebels attacked cities; they disturbed Ami as well; he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin'an Hui rebels attacked cities and spread to Ami, he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 九年，省回就撫後，踞碧雞關，劫奪近郊，分剿乃散。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, after the provincial Hui had submitted to pacification, they occupied Biji Pass and plundered the nearby suburbs; he sent detachments to suppress them and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, after capital Hui had submitted, some occupied Biji Pass and raided the suburbs until detachments dispersed them.

sentences.zh: 又剿平彝、安寧、緬寧、楚雄諸匪，武定、羅次、富民、祿豐、祿勸諸州縣先後克復。

translations.literal: He also suppressed bandits in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong; the prefectures and counties of Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan were recovered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also suppressed rebels in Yi, Anning, Mianning, and Chuxiong, and recovered Wuding, Luoci, Fumin, Lufeng, and Luquan in turn.

sentences.zh: 然回、練互相猜忌，亂機時起。

translations.literal: Yet Hui and militia mutually suspected one another, and outbreaks of disorder arose from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hui and militia remained mutually suspicious, and unrest broke out repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 徐之銘既為巡撫，貪縱險狠，與亮基陰不相能，時構煽其間。

translations.literal: Once Xu Zhiming became governor he was greedy, indulgent, fierce, and treacherous; he and Liangji secretly could not get along and constantly stirred trouble between them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Zhiming became governor, his greed, cruelty, and treachery put him at odds with Liangji, and he constantly stirred trouble between them.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，回人掌教馬德新、徐元吉，武生馬現，率各屬回民來省乞撫，住城外江右館，亮基約之銘同詣撫諭。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year the Hui religious teacher Ma Dexin, Xu Yuanji, and military licentiate Ma Xian led Hui from various districts to the provincial capital to beg pacification and lodged at the Jiangyou Lodge outside the walls; Liangji invited Zhiming to go together to pacify and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1860, Ma Dexin, Xu Yuanji, and Ma Xian led Hui from the districts to the capital to seek pacification and lodged at the Jiangyou Lodge outside the walls; Liangji asked Zhiming to join him in receiving them.

sentences.zh: 之銘陰嗾已散練丁擁至督署阻撓，諭之不可，殺通海知縣雷焱於門，遂逼殺招撫委員紳士馬椿齡、孫鈞。

translations.literal: Zhiming secretly incited already disbanded militiamen to crowd to the governor-general's yamen and obstruct proceedings; they could not be instructed otherwise; they killed Tonghai District Magistrate Lei Yan at the gate, and then forced the killing of pacification commissioners and gentry Ma Chunling and Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiming secretly roused disbanded militiamen to block the governor-general's yamen; they would not listen, killed Tonghai Magistrate Lei Yan at the gate, and then murdered pacification commissioners Ma Chunling and Sun Jun.

sentences.zh: 亮基為所脅持，不敢入告，以病乞罷，命劉源灝代之。

translations.literal: Liangji was coerced by them and dared not enter to report; he asked to retire on grounds of illness, and Liu Yuanhao was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Coerced by the mob, Liangji dared not report the affair; he resigned on grounds of illness, and Liu Yuanhao was appointed to replace him.

sentences.zh: 源灝久不至，亮基迳去。

translations.literal: Yuanhao long failed to arrive, and Liangji departed directly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao failed to arrive, Liangji left without waiting.

sentences.zh: 十一年，至湖北，乃疏陳滇事，劾之銘不法。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when he reached Hubei, he then memorialized on affairs in Yunnan and impeached Zhiming for unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, reaching Hubei, he memorialized on Yunnan affairs and impeached Zhiming for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 會布政使鄧爾恆升任陝西巡撫，去滇，之銘嗾匪戕於路。

translations.literal: At the same time Provincial Administration Commissioner Deng Erheng was promoted to governor of Shaanxi; as he left Yunnan, Zhiming incited bandits to kill him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Provincial Administration Commissioner Deng Erheng was promoted to Shaanxi and left Yunnan, Zhiming incited bandits to murder him on the road.

sentences.zh: 於是罷源灝，以潘鐸署總督，命亮基赴滇查辦，督師剿匪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanhao was dismissed; Pan Duo was appointed acting governor-general; Liangji was ordered to go to Yunnan to investigate and handle affairs and to command troops in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao was dismissed, Pan Duo was made acting governor-general, and Liangji was ordered to Yunnan to investigate the situation and command troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 亮基疏請發部照募損充餉，募勇千人然後行，與潘鐸先後至四川，欲資其餉力、兵力。

translations.literal: Liangji memorialized requesting ministry authorization to raise funds through the donation-for-office system to supplement military pay, to recruit a thousand braves before departing, and he and Pan Duo reached Sichuan in succession, intending to draw on its pay resources and military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji asked for ministry authorization to raise funds through office sales and to recruit a thousand braves before setting out; he and Pan Duo reached Sichuan in turn, hoping to draw on its funds and troops.

sentences.zh: 四川兵事未定，無以濟之。

translations.literal: Military affairs in Sichuan were unsettled, and there was no way to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's own war was still unsettled, and nothing could be spared to help.

sentences.zh: 林自清者，亮基之舊部，方署雲南提督，與之銘及馬如龍等皆不協，回人仇之。

translations.literal: Lin Ziqing was Liangji's former subordinate, then acting provincial military commander of Yunnan; he could not get along with Zhiming, Ma Rulong, and others, and the Hui bore him enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Ziqing, Liangji's former subordinate and acting provincial commander of Yunnan, was at odds with Zhiming, Ma Rulong, and others, and the Hui hated him.

sentences.zh: 聞亮基在四川，擅率所部號萬人入川求效用，阻之不聽。

translations.literal: Hearing that Liangji was in Sichuan, he on his own authority led his command, which he claimed numbered ten thousand, into Sichuan to seek employment; they were blocked but would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Liangji was in Sichuan, he led his troops—claiming ten thousand men—into the province on his own authority to offer his services; they were stopped but refused to turn back.

sentences.zh: 詔亮基撫諭解散，而之銘嗾馬如龍等聲言拒亮基不使入境，相持久之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liangji to pacify and instruct them to disband, but Zhiming incited Ma Rulong and others to proclaim that they would refuse Liangji and not let him enter the border; the standoff dragged on.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Liangji to pacify the force and send it home, but Zhiming incited Ma Rulong and others to declare they would bar Liangji from entering Yunnan, and the deadlock continued.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，潘鐸先抵任，請暫留之銘以畢撫局，遂改命亮基以總督銜署貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Pan Duo arrived first to take up his post and requested that Zhiming be temporarily retained to complete the pacification arrangement; Liangji was then reassigned to serve as acting governor of Guizhou with the rank of governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 Pan Duo took up his post first and asked that Zhiming be kept on to finish the pacification; Liangji was reassigned as acting governor of Guizhou with governor-general rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，之銘复陰嗾回眾​​為變，鐸被戕，而雲南之亂愈亟矣。

translations.literal: Before long Zhiming again secretly incited the Hui masses to revolt; Duo was killed, and the disorder in Yunnan grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhiming again secretly roused the Hui to revolt; Pan Duo was murdered, and the chaos in Yunnan grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 二年，亮基至貴州，黃號、白號、苗、教諸匪並熾，上下游遍地皆賊。

translations.literal: In the second year Liangji reached Guizhou; Yellow Banner, White Banner, Miao, and sect bandits all flared up together, and upriver and downriver the land was overrun with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Liangji reached Guizhou; Yellow Banner, White Banner, Miao, and sect rebels were all on the rise, and bandits filled the province from headwaters to lowlands.

sentences.zh: 亮基令總兵沈宏富等攻遵義螺螄堰，破之，殲餘匪於上稽場。

translations.literal: Liangji ordered Regional Commander Shen Hongfu and others to attack the Snail Embankment at Zunyi, broke it, and annihilated the remaining bandits at Shangji Field.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji sent Regional Commander Shen Hongfu and others against the Snail Embankment at Zunyi, took it, and wiped out the survivors at Shangji Field.

sentences.zh: 令總兵劉義方等剿思南教匪，复普安、安南，又連破苗匪於桐梓鼎城及水城廳馬龍胯，擒匪首何潤科等於黔西，降萬人。

translations.literal: He ordered Regional Commander Liu Yifang and others to suppress sect bandits in Sinan, recovered Pu'an and Annan, and in succession broke Miao bandits at Dingcheng in Tongzi and Malongkuai in Shuicheng Department, captured bandit chiefs He Runke and others in western Guizhou, and received the surrender of ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Regional Commander Liu Yifang against the sect rebels in Sinan, recovered Pu'an and Annan, then broke Miao bands at Dingcheng in Tongzi and Malongkuai in Shuicheng, captured the chief He Runke and others in western Guizhou, and accepted ten thousand surrenders.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚大坪匪犯省城，督沈宏富等戰於郊，殲賊千計，復修文。

translations.literal: In the third year bandits from Shangdaping threatened the provincial capital; he directed Shen Hongfu and others to fight in the suburbs, destroyed several thousand rebels, and recovered Xiuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year rebels from Shangdaping threatened the capital; he led Shen Hongfu and others in a suburban battle, killed several thousand, and recovered Xiuwen.

sentences.zh: 總兵林自清、趙德昌克龍里，又復興義，解清鎮之圍，收復定番、廣順、長寨諸城，破龍泉、湄潭黃、白號匪老巢，克滇西衛城。

translations.literal: Regional Commanders Lin Ziqing and Zhao Dechang captured Longli, also recovered Xingyi, relieved the siege of Qingzhen, recovered the cities of Dingfan, Guangshun, Changzhai, and others, broke the old lairs of Yellow and White Banner bandits at Longquan and Meitan, and captured the garrison city of Dianxiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Ziqing and Zhao Dechang took Longli, recovered Xingyi, lifted the siege of Qingzhen, retook Dingfan, Guangshun, Changzhai, and other towns, destroyed Yellow and White Banner strongholds at Longquan and Meitan, and captured the Dianxiwei garrison.

sentences.zh: 四年，克黔西石阡、永寧、荔波，貴州地瘠財匱，飢軍索餉，時虞譁噪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they captured Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo in western Guizhou; Guizhou's land was poor and funds scarce, starving troops demanded pay, and mutinous clamor was constantly feared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they took Shiqian, Yongning, and Libo in western Guizhou; the province was poor and funds short, hungry troops clamored for pay, and mutiny was feared at any moment.

sentences.zh: 亮基撫馭防剿，僅得粗安，而所部諸將多驕蹇，輿論不協，為侍讀學士景其濬論劾。

translations.literal: Liangji pacified, controlled, and guarded against suppression and barely achieved rough stability, but many generals under his command were arrogant and obstinate, public opinion was at odds, and Academician Reader Jing Qijun memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji held the province together by pacification and defense, achieving only rough stability; many of his generals were arrogant and insubordinate, opinion turned against him, and Academician Reader Jing Qijun impeached him.

sentences.zh: 亮基乃劾總兵林自清、劉有勳，副將池有連等劫掠扣餉，不聽調度，請嚴治。

translations.literal: Liangji then impeached Regional Commanders Lin Ziqing and Liu Youxun and Vice Commanders Chi Youlian and others for plundering and withholding pay and disobeying command, requesting severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji in turn impeached Lin Ziqing, Liu Youxun, Chi Youlian, and others for looting, withholding pay, and defying orders, and asked that they be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 詔布政使嚴樹森察奏，亮基復具疏自陳，言樹森規避貴州，安坐鄰省不親至，於是亮基、樹森並褫職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Yan Shusen to investigate and report; Liangji again submitted a full memorial in his own defense, stating that Shusen evaded Guizhou and sat at ease in a neighboring province without coming in person; thereupon both Liangji and Shusen were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Provincial Commissioner Yan Shusen to investigate; Liangji countered with a memorial accusing Shusen of avoiding Guizhou and staying in a neighboring province; both men were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫王文韶、貴州巡撫曾璧光先後請復原銜，各建專祠。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Wang Wenshao and Guizhou Governor Zeng Biguang successively requested restoration of his original rank, and each province built a dedicated shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Wang Wenshao of Hunan and Zeng Biguang of Guizhou successively asked that his former rank be restored, and each province built him a shrine.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十四年，湖南、貴州京官合詞臚陳功德在民，追諡惠肅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu, Beijing officials from Hunan and Guizhou jointly memorialized enumerating his merits among the people, and he was posthumously given the temple name Huisu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908 officials from Hunan and Guizhou in Beijing jointly memorialized on his public service, and he was posthumously given the temple name Huisu.

sentences.zh: =毛鴻賓=毛鴻賓，字翊雲，山東歷城人。

translations.literal: =Mao Hongbin= Mao Hongbin, courtesy name Yiyun, a native of Licheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: =Mao Hongbin= Mao Hongbin, courtesy name Yiyun, was a native of Licheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1838, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中，數上封事論軍務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary and several times submitted sealed memorials discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to censor and supervising secretary and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，以尚書孫瑞珍薦，命回籍治團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, on the recommendation of Minister Sun Ruizhen, he was ordered to return to his native place to organize local militia.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, on Minister Sun Ruizhen's recommendation, he was ordered home to organize local militia.

sentences.zh: 四年，劾幫辦軍務大臣勝保罪狀，請嚴旨查辦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he impeached Assistant Grand Councilor for Military Affairs Shengbao for his crimes and requested a stern edict for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he impeached Assistant Grand Councilor Shengbao and asked for a stern edict to investigate and punish him.

sentences.zh: 五年，授湖北荊宜施道，調安襄鄖荊道，歷安徽按察使、江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed intendant of the Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit in Hubei, transferred to the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit, and successively served as judicial commissioner of Anhui and provincial administration commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made intendant of the Jing-Yi-Shi Circuit in Hubei, then of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit, and later served as Anhui judicial commissioner and Jiangsu administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署湖南巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting governor of Hunan and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was acting governor of Hunan and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「湖南地居僻遠，向非富強，自前撫臣張亮基、駱秉章等於吏治民風實力講求，用能削平寇盜，屹為上游重鎮，用人之效，有明徵矣。

translations.literal: He memorialized, stating: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has not traditionally been wealthy or strong; since former governors Zhang Liangji, Luo Zongzhang, and others applied themselves thoroughly to official governance and local customs, they were able to cut down bandits and rebels and make it stand firm as a great stronghold of the upper reaches; the effect of employing the right men has clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Hunan lies in a remote corner and has never been wealthy or strong; yet former governors Zhang Liangji and Luo Zongzhang worked hard at governance and local custom, cut down bandits, and made the province a pillar of the upper Yangzi—the proof that good appointments matter is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 臣以為名將不過收戰陣之功，得賢督撫，斯能造封疆之福。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that famous generals achieve no more than battlefield merit; with worthy governors and governors-general, one can bring blessing to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that famous generals win no more than battlefield glory; it takes worthy governors and governors-general to bring peace and prosperity to a province.

sentences.zh: 如左宗棠識略過人，其才力不在曾國籓、胡林翼之下，今但使之帶勇，殊不足以盡其長，倘畀以封疆重任，必能保境安民，兼顧大局。

translations.literal: Such as Zuo Zongtang, whose strategic vision surpasses ordinary men and whose talent and strength are not below those of Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi: now he is only made to lead braves, which is quite insufficient to exhaust his strengths; if entrusted with a weighty frontier post, he would surely be able to secure the territory and pacify the people while also attending to the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang's vision surpasses ordinary men; his ability matches Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi. Yet he is only allowed to lead troops, which wastes his gifts; give him a major frontier post and he will secure the province, calm the people, and serve the larger cause.

sentences.zh: 前任雲貴總督張亮基，果決有為，雲南壤接邊陲，餉糈不給，漢、回仇釁相尋，即令經營盡善，亦僅有益一隅，似不若任以要地，俾展所長。

translations.literal: The former governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou Zhang Liangji is resolute and capable; Yunnan's territory adjoins the frontier, pay and grain are not supplied, and Han-Hui enmity follows in succession; even if management were wholly excellent, it would benefit only one corner; it seems better not to assign him to a key post and let him display his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Former governor-general Zhang Liangji is resolute and capable, but Yunnan borders foreign lands, pay is short, and Han-Hui strife never ends; even perfect management there would help only one corner. Better assign him to a key post where he can do his best work.

sentences.zh: 但使東南日有轉機，則云、貴遊氛無難迅掃，此輕重之機宜審者也。」

translations.literal: If only the southeast daily gained a turning point, then the roaming miasma of Yunnan and Guizhou would be no hard matter to sweep away swiftly; this is a matter of weighing priorities that must be carefully considered."
translations.idiomatic: If the southeast turns the corner, the unrest in Yunnan and Guizhou can be swept away quickly—that is why one must weigh priorities carefully."

sentences.zh: 時湘軍所至有功，各省多往召募，鴻賓疏陳招勇流弊，請慎選將領以收實效，並被嘉納。

translations.literal: At that time wherever the Hunan Army went it achieved merit, and many provinces went to recruit from it; Hongbin memorialized setting forth the abuses of recruiting braves and requested careful selection of commanders to obtain real effect, and this was also commended and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Hunan armies were winning wherever they fought, and provinces rushed to recruit from them; Hongbin warned of the abuses of indiscriminate recruiting and asked that commanders be chosen carefully for real results, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 石達開竄湖南，鴻賓遣知府席寶田、副將周達武、總兵趙福元分路進擊，解會同、黔陽之圍。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled into Hunan; Hongbin dispatched Prefect Xi Baotian, Vice Commander Zhou Dawu, and Regional Commander Zhao Fuyuan to advance by separate routes and attack, relieving the sieges of Huitong and Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai fled into Hunan, Hongbin sent Prefect Xi Baotian, Vice Commander Zhou Dawu, and Regional Commander Zhao Fuyuan by separate routes, lifting the sieges of Huitong and Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，進復來鳳，貴州提督田興恕兼署巡撫，軍報不實，信用左右，鴻賓疏劾之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he advanced and recovered Laifeng; Guizhou Provincial Military Commander Tian Xingyu also served as acting governor, his military reports were untrue, and he trusted those at his side; Hongbin memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he recovered Laifeng; Guizhou commander Tian Xingyu, also acting governor, filed false reports and trusted his favorites, and Hongbin impeached him.

sentences.zh: 遣兵越境剿貴州竄匪，复天柱縣城。

translations.literal: He dispatched troops across the border to suppress bandits who had fled into Guizhou and recovered Tiancheng County seat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops across the border against Guizhou rebels and recovered Tiancheng.

sentences.zh: 又剿銅仁張家寨，匪首蕭文魁率眾降，克大小青兩堡。

translations.literal: He also suppressed Zhang Family Stockade in Tongren; bandit chief Xiao Wenkui led the crowd to surrender, and the two forts of Daqing and Xiaoqing were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Zhang Family Stockade in Tongren; the chief Xiao Wenkui surrendered with his men, and the Daqing and Xiaoqing forts were taken.

sentences.zh: 江藍廳同知椿齡指團紳為土匪，鴻賓廉知椿齡有酷刑逼借事，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Jianglan Department Subprefect Chunling denounced militia gentry as bandits; Hongbin, having learned that Chunling had used cruel torture to force loans, impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Subprefect Chunling of Jianglan Department denounced militia leaders as bandits; Hongbin found he had tortured men to extort loans and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 椿齡京控，訐鴻賓借貸不遂，鴻賓自請查辦，下總督官文鞫訊，得白。

translations.literal: Chunling appealed to Beijing, accusing Hongbin of failing to obtain a loan; Hongbin asked on his own to be investigated; the case was sent down to Governor-General Guan Wen for examination, and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Chunling appealed in Beijing, claiming Hongbin had retaliated over a refused loan; Hongbin asked for an inquiry; Governor-General Guan Wen tried the case and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 擢兩廣總督，英德土匪起，令按察使張運蘭剿平之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; bandits rose in Yingde, and he ordered Judicial Commissioner Zhang Yunlan to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to governor-general of the two Guangs, he sent Judicial Commissioner Zhang Yunlan to crush bandits who had risen in Yingde.

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫郭嵩燾奏定變通緝捕章程，獲大盜者予優擢，允之。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Guo Songtao he memorialized and established revised regulations for pursuit and arrest; those who captured great bandits were to receive preferential promotion. This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Governor Guo Songtao he drew up flexible regulations for pursuit and arrest, with preferential promotion for the capture of major bandits. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，江南既复，浙、贛餘氛未靖。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangnan had already been recovered, but lingering unrest in Zhejiang and Jiangxi had not yet been pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, though Jiangnan had been recovered, unrest still lingered in Zhejiang and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓疏言：「江西南路之防猶有未備，閩、粵交界均無防兵，慮賊上竄，以粵東為尾閭。

translations.literal: Hongbin memorialized, stating: "The defenses of southern Jiangxi are still incomplete; along the Fujian-Guangdong border there are no defensive troops at all. I fear the bandits will flee upward, taking eastern Guangdong as their final outlet.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin memorialized: "Southern Jiangxi remains inadequately defended, and along the Fujian-Guangdong border there are no troops at all. I fear the rebels will flee northward and make eastern Guangdong their last refuge.

sentences.zh: 江西當四沖之地，宜合數省兵力，乘大勝餘威，聚而殲之。

translations.literal: Jiangxi stands where four routes converge; it is fitting to combine forces from several provinces, ride the remaining prestige of the great victory, gather together, and annihilate them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi sits at a crossroads of four routes; we should combine troops from several provinces, press our advantage while victory is fresh, and destroy them in one concentrated strike.

sentences.zh: 已諮曾國籓調撥勁旅，繞越寧郡、石城一帶，扼賊南竄之路，臣派一軍於閩、粵交界會同進剿。

translations.literal: I have already consulted Zeng Guofan to transfer crack troops, detouring through Ning Prefecture, Shicheng, and the surrounding region to block the bandits' route of flight southward; your servant will dispatch one army to the Fujian-Guangdong border to join in the advance to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: I have already asked Zeng Guofan to send crack troops around Ning Prefecture and Shicheng to block the rebels' southern escape routes; I will dispatch a force to the Fujian-Guangdong border to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 並請敕曾國籓嚴守南贛，俾毋竄越。」

translations.literal: I also request that an imperial order instruct Zeng Guofan to guard southern Gan strictly so that they may not flee across the border."
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that the court order Zeng Guofan to hold southern Gan firmly so the rebels cannot slip through."

sentences.zh: 四年，坐前在湖南，道員胡鏞請諮引見，繳回咨文，委署道缺，降一級調用，回籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of a prior matter when in Hunan—when circuit intendant Hu Yong requested consultation for an imperial audience, the memorial of inquiry was returned, he had been entrusted with acting in a circuit post—he was reduced one rank and transferred elsewhere and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was punished for an earlier affair in Hunan, when Intendant Hu Yong had sought permission for an imperial audience: the referral was withdrawn, an acting circuit post was voided, he was demoted one rank and transferred, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，山東巡撫袁樹勳疏陳鴻賓功績，復原官，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuantong reign the Shandong governor Yuan Shuxun memorialized Hongbin's achievements; his original office was restored and he was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuantong, Shandong Governor Yuan Shuxun memorialized Hongbin's achievements; his former rank was restored and he was entered in the local worthies' shrine.

sentences.zh: =張凱嵩=張凱嵩，字云卿，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: =Zhang Kaisong= Zhang Kaisong, courtesy name Yunqing, a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: =Zhang Kaisong= Zhang Kaisong, courtesy name Yunqing, was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，廣西即用知縣，歷宣化、懷集、臨桂知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed expectancy magistrate in Guangxi, and successively served as magistrate of Xuanhua, Huaiji, and Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, he was appointed expectancy magistrate in Guangxi and served successively as magistrate of Xuanhua, Huaiji, and Lingui.

sentences.zh: 李星沅、勞崇光並薦其能，咸豐五年，擢慶遠知府。

translations.literal: Li Xingyuan and Lao Chongguang both recommended his ability; in the fifth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to prefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingyuan and Lao Chongguang both praised his talents; in the fifth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Prefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 剿平土匪王得勝等，擢左江道，調署右江道。

translations.literal: He suppressed and pacified the bandits Wang Desheng and others, was promoted to intendant of the Left River Circuit, and transferred to act as intendant of the Right River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After suppressing bandits such as Wang Desheng, he was promoted to Intendant of the Left River Circuit and transferred to act as Intendant of the Right River Circuit.

sentences.zh: 慶遠失守，革職留任。

translations.literal: When Qingyuan fell he was dismissed from office but retained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingyuan fell he was stripped of rank but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕按察使蔣益澧破賊，克慶遠，復原官，署按察使，尋實授，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with judicial commissioner Jiang Yizao he defeated the bandits, recovered Qingyuan, was restored to his original office, acted as judicial commissioner, was soon appointed in substantive capacity, and was transferred to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he and Judicial Commissioner Jiang Yizao defeated the rebels, retook Qingyuan, was restored to office, served as acting and then substantive judicial commissioner, and rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，巡撫劉長佑赴潯州籌剿撫，留凱嵩經畫後路。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Governor Liu Changyou went to Xunzhou to plan suppression and pacification; Kaisong was left to arrange the rear routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, Governor Liu Changyou went to Xunzhou to direct pacification; Kaisong was left to manage logistics on the rear lines.

sentences.zh: 荔浦張皋友陷陽朔，遣兵敗賊於鷓鴣岩，復其城，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Zhang Gaoyou of Lipu seized Yangshuo; he dispatched troops and defeated the bandits at Partridge Rock Pass, recovered the city, and was thereupon promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gaoyou of Lipu seized Yangshuo; Kaisong sent troops, routed the rebels at Partridge Rock Pass, recovered the city, and was promptly promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 諸匪中黃鼎鳳、張皋友最猖獗，分陷貴縣、陽朔、麕集大鹿灘、馬瀨，檄總兵李明惠、提督江忠義先剿馬瀨，進規貴縣，破之於桂嶺，殲擒賊首張皋友、陳土養。

translations.literal: Among all the bandits Huang Dingfeng and Zhang Gaoyou were the most rampant; they separately seized Guixian, Yangshuo, massed at Dalutan, and Malai. He ordered Regional Commander Li Minghui and Provincial Commander Jiang Zhongyi first to suppress Malai and then advance against Guixian; he defeated them at Guiling and annihilated and captured the rebel leaders Zhang Gaoyou and Chen Tuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dingfeng and Zhang Gaoyou were the fiercest among the rebels, overrunning Guixian, Yangshuo, Dalutan, and Malai. He ordered Regional Commander Li Minghui and Provincial Commander Jiang Zhongyi to clear Malai first, then advance on Guixian; at Guiling he routed them and killed or captured Zhang Gaoyou and Chen Tuyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，檄布政使劉坤一攻黃鼎鳳於登龍橋。

translations.literal: In the second year he issued orders to administration commissioner Liu Kunyi to attack Huang Dingfeng at Denglong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he ordered Administration Commissioner Liu Kunyi to attack Huang Dingfeng at Denglong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊走覃塘，進圍之。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Qintang; he advanced and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Qintang and he pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 信都賊陳金剛等來援，道員蔣澤春逆擊敗之，進克容縣，坤一克覃塘。

translations.literal: The Xindu bandits Chen Jingang and others came to their aid; circuit intendant Jiang Zechun met and defeated them, advanced and recovered Rong County, and Kunyi took Qintang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingang of Xindu and others marched to relieve the siege; Intendant Jiang Zechun intercepted and routed them, recovered Rong County, and Kunyi took Qintang.

sentences.zh: 三年，克天平寨，擒黃鼎鳳。

translations.literal: In the third year he took Tianping Stockade and captured Huang Dingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he seized Tianping Stockade and captured Huang Dingfeng.

sentences.zh: 貴縣平，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: When Guixian was pacified he was granted an elevated honorary cap button.
translations.idiomatic: With Guixian pacified, he was granted an elevated honorary cap button as Qing rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 疏陳左右江積匪未清，議三路進兵，以劉坤一統七營留防潯州，易元泰統十一營由賓州、遷江達思恩，李士恩統水陸八營由橫州達南寧，節節進剿。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that accumulated bandits on the Left and Right Rivers had not yet been cleared; he proposed advancing by three routes—Liu Kunyi commanding seven battalions to remain and defend Xunzhou, Yi Yuantai commanding eleven battalions from Binxian and Qianjiang to reach Si'en, and Li Shien commanding eight land and water battalions from Hengzhou to reach Nanning—advancing step by step to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that banditry still festered on the Left and Right Rivers and proposed a three-pronged advance: Liu Kunyi with seven battalions to hold Xunzhou, Yi Yuantai with eleven battalions through Binxian and Qianjiang toward Si'en, and Li Shien with eight land and water battalions from Hengzhou toward Nanning, pressing forward in stages.

sentences.zh: 四年，坤一攻克大廟、江口、平菼，斬賊首梁安邦，南寧河道始通。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Kunyi captured Damiao, Jiangkou, and Pingqin, beheaded the rebel leader Liang Anbang, and the Nanning river route was at last open.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Kunyi took Damiao, Jiangkou, and Pingqin, beheaded the rebel leader Liang Anbang, and the waterways to Nanning were finally open.

sentences.zh: 元泰剿上林，平之。

translations.literal: Yuantai suppressed Shanglin and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuantai suppressed Shanglin and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 坤一擢江西巡撫去，以同知劉培一代領其軍，將親赴南寧督戰，會偽康王汪海洋竄粵，將入廣西，詔凱嵩駐防潯州。

translations.literal: Kunyi was promoted to governor of Jiangxi and departed; subprefect Liu Peiyi took command of his army in his stead. Kaisong was about to go in person to Nanning to direct the campaign when the false Prince Kang Wang Wang Haiyang fled into Guangdong and was about to enter Guangxi; an edict ordered Kaisong to garrison and defend Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi was promoted to Jiangxi governor and departed; Subprefect Liu Peiyi took over his forces. Kaisong was preparing to lead the campaign at Nanning in person when the Taiping Prince Kang Wang Wang Haiyang fled into Guangdong and threatened Guangxi; the court ordered Kaisong to hold Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，凱嵩至南寧，進攻山澤，督諸軍穴地轟城，奪山入，擒偽平章蘇仲熙等。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Kaisong reached Nanning, advanced to attack Shanzhe, supervised the armies in tunneling and bombarding the walls, seized the heights and entered, and captured the false chancellor Su Zhongxi and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Kaisong reached Nanning, attacked Shanzhe, directed his troops in mining and breaching the walls, stormed the heights, and captured the Taiping chancellor Su Zhongxi and others.

sentences.zh: 孫仁廣單騎走旺隴，追斬之。

translations.literal: Sun Renguang fled alone on horseback to Wanglong; he was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renguang fled alone toward Wanglong and was run down and killed.

sentences.zh: 山澤為賊所踞十餘年，至此悉平。

translations.literal: Shanzhe had been occupied by bandits for more than ten years; by this time it was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhe had been held by rebels for more than a decade; at last it was wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 自潘鐸被戕，滇事益紛。

translations.literal: Since Pan Duo was assassinated, affairs in Yunnan grew ever more chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Since Pan Duo's assassination, Yunnan affairs had grown ever more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 行至巴東，稱病，三疏請罷，坐規避，褫職。

translations.literal: When he reached Badong he claimed illness and three times memorialized to resign; he was convicted of evasion, stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Badong he pleaded illness and thrice asked to be relieved; convicted of shirking duty, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，以五品京堂起用，授通政使參議，遷內閣侍讀學士，署順天府尹，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was recalled to service as a fifth-rank official at court, appointed counselor of the Office of Transmission, transferred to reader in the Grand Secretariat, acted as governor of Shuntian Prefecture, and appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was recalled as a fifth-rank capital official, made Counselor of the Office of Transmission, promoted to Reader in the Grand Secretariat, served as acting Governor of Shuntian, and was appointed Governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 請於省城設開採五金總局，以興礦利，偕內閣學士周德潤勘越南界務。

translations.literal: He requested establishing at the provincial capital a general bureau for mining the five metals to promote mineral profits, and together with Grand Secretariat academician Zhou Derun surveyed the Vietnam border.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a provincial bureau to develop the five metals and revive mining revenues, and joined Grand Secretariat Academician Zhou Derun in surveying the Vietnam border.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫李秉衡疏陳凱嵩政績，請建專祠，廣西京官論其不當，罷之。

translations.literal: The Guangxi governor Li Bingheng memorialized Kaisong's administrative achievements and requested a dedicated shrine; Guangxi officials at the capital argued that this was improper, and the request was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Governor Li Bingheng memorialized Kaisong's record and asked for a private shrine; Guangxi officials in Beijing objected, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 子仲炘，光緒三年進士，由翰林御史官至通政司參議，敢言有聲。

translations.literal: His son Zhongxin, a jinshi of the third year of Guangxu, rose from Hanlin censor to counselor of the Office of Transmission and was famed for bold speech.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongxin, a jinshi of the third year of Guangxu, rose from Hanlin censor to Counselor of the Office of Transmission and won renown for outspoken memorials.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：雲南地居邊遠，回、漢積仇，中原多故之秋，幾為王靈所不及。

translations.literal: =Commentary= Commentary: Yunnan lies on a distant frontier; Han and Hui bore long-standing enmity; in an autumn when the central plains were beset with troubles, it nearly lay beyond the reach of imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: =Commentary= Commentary: Yunnan lay on a distant frontier where Han and Hui nursed old hatreds; while the heartland was torn by troubles, the province nearly slipped beyond imperial reach.

sentences.zh: 吳振棫兼籌剿撫，實體中朝措置之難。

translations.literal: Wu Zhenyu combined planning for suppression and pacification, truly embodying the difficulty of the court's arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenyu had to balance suppression and pacification at once—a fair measure of how hard the court's task was.

sentences.zh: 張亮基才足有為，誤用徐之銘，受其排擠，遂至不可收拾。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji had talent enough to achieve things, but misused Xu Zhiming, suffered his ostracism, and affairs thereupon became beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji was capable enough to make a difference, but misused Xu Zhiming, was driven out by him, and the situation became irremediable.

sentences.zh: 自潘鐸被戕之後，無人敢任其艱危。

translations.literal: After Pan Duo was assassinated, no one dared undertake its peril.
translations.idiomatic: After Pan Duo's murder, no one would take on so perilous a post.

sentences.zh: 毛鴻賓疏言內地寇平，邊方自靖，誠為確論。

translations.literal: Mao Hongbin's memorial that when internal banditry was pacified the frontier would quiet itself was indeed a sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongbin was right to argue that once inland rebellion was crushed, the borderlands would settle of themselves.

sentences.zh: 張凱嵩因規避黜，後仍以舊勞起用，朝廷固鑑其情已。

translations.literal: Zhang Kaisong was dismissed for evasion, yet later was recalled on account of past service; the court had indeed taken the measure of his circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kaisong was cashiered for shirking duty, yet later restored for past service—the court had long understood his situation.
